newsitem.title: RWANDA: Aid agency attacked in southwestern Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Aid agency attacked in southwestern Rwanda.

text.p: Unidentified attackers made a half-hearted assault on the compound of the Spanish wing of an international aid agency in southwestern Rwanda, aid officials said on Tuesday.

But they said the Monday attack, the third on Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) in Rwanda in two weeks, led them to believe they were being deliberately targeted more than a week after three Spanish aid workers were shot dead in the northwest.
The latest attack was on the MSF-Spain compound in the southwestern town of Cyangugu, 400 km (250) miles from Kigali.
"At about seven o'clock in the evening on Monday the compound was attacked by two men in some form of uniform, at least one of whom was armed," said Steffi Tarade, an MSF official in Kigali.

"There was a great deal of screaming. Curiously one of the attackers ran away and the other one was disarmed by our unarmed guard," she said. Rwandan security forces arrived three to four minutes after the MSF team contacted the U.N. refugee agency.
"Somehow after the arrest, the assailant managed to get shot in the leg. Until we can prove to the contrary we can only assume that we are being deliberately targeted," said Tarade.
There were no casualties in the previous two attacks on MSF.

Rwandan officials said troops killed some 80 people in a crackdown in the northeastern prefecture of Ruhengeri last week after suspected Hutu militiamen killed three Spanish aid workers of Medicos del Mundo (Doctors of the World) in their compound.

In the same attack an American aid worker was shot in one of his legs which was amputated. The aid workers' killings followed a series of attacks on survivors of the 1994 genocide and Hutu witnesses to the killings who had returned to Rwanda in November and December.
It was the worst deliberate attack on foreigners in Rwanda since the an estimated 800,000 ethnic Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed by hardline Hutu militiamen and troops in 1994.
Gunmen stormed a house where the aid workers were staying and demanded their passports before shooting the three Spaniards -- two men and a woman nurse -- at close range in their heads.

Following the killings, the United Nations said aid work in Ruhengeri would be limited to the daytime and expatriate workers would not be allowed to spend a night in the city, close to Zaire's border.
